title: Flat comparison of filtered cochain complexes
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $(C^\bullet,F)$ be a bounded-below cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with a finite, exhaustive decreasing filtration by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration], and let $(D^\bullet,F)$ be such a filtered complex of $B$-modules. Suppose $u:C^\bullet\otimes_A B\to D^\bullet$ is a filtered cochain map. For the convergent spectral sequences [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] of these filtrations, flatness canonically identifies every page $E_r(C\otimes_A B)$ with $E_r(C)\otimes_A B$, compatibly with differentials. If the induced map $E_2^{p,q}(C)\otimes_A B\to E_2^{p,q}(D)$ is an isomorphism for every $(p,q)$, then $H^n(u):H^n(C)\otimes_A B\to H^n(D)$ is an isomorphism for every $n$.

source.place: Tag 0BDU, definition-spectral-sequence, and lemma-spectral-sequence-filtered-complex-functorial; applied in Cohomology of Schemes, Tag 02KH, quasi-separated case

proof.text: Apply the functorial filtered-complex spectral-sequence construction [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] to the filtered complexes C and C\otimes_A B; the filtration F^pC\otimes_A B is a filtration of C\otimes_A B by subcomplexes because tensoring with the flat A-module B preserves the injections F^{p+1}C\to F^pC\to C [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], and it is again finite. By right exactness of the tensor product, gr^p(C\otimes_A B)=(gr^pC)\otimes_A B. The canonical map H^{p+q}(gr^pC)\otimes_A B\to H^{p+q}((gr^pC)\otimes_A B) is an isomorphism by [lem-pc-flat-tensor-complex-cohom] (an elementary remark: $H^i$ of a complex depends only on its terms in degrees $i-1,i,i+1$, so one applies the cited lemma to the bounded stupid truncation $0\to K^{i-1}\to K^i\to K^{i+1}\to0$, which has the same $H^i$ and commutes with $-\otimes_A B$); it is compatible with the boundary maps d_1 by naturality. Thus the E_1-page of C\otimes_A B is canonically E_1(C)\otimes_A B, compatibly with d_1.

source.place: Tag 0BDU, definition-spectral-sequence, and the filtered-complex construction; flat tensor exactness in the proof of Tag 02KH

proof.text: Induct on r. Suppose the canonical map E_r(C)\otimes_A B\to E_r(C\otimes_A B) is an isomorphism and commutes with d_r. By [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] (a), E_{r+1} is naturally the cohomology of the page complex (E_r,d_r). Since the filtration is finite, each page complex through a given bidegree has only finitely many nonzero terms, and [lem-pc-flat-tensor-complex-cohom] (an elementary remark: $H^i$ of a complex depends only on its terms in degrees $i-1,i,i+1$, so one applies the cited lemma to the bounded stupid truncation $0\to K^{i-1}\to K^i\to K^{i+1}\to0$, which has the same $H^i$ and commutes with $-\otimes_A B$) gives E_{r+1}(C)\otimes_A B\cong H(E_r(C)\otimes_A B,d_r\otimes1)\cong E_{r+1}(C\otimes_A B), compatibly with the page identifications. This proves the asserted canonical identification on every page. The filtered map u gives a morphism of these spectral sequences by the functoriality clause (c) of [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields]. Its E_2 map is an isomorphism by hypothesis, so by [lem-sp-page-induction] it is an isomorphism on every page E_r, r\geq2, and on E_\infty (for the finite filtration the pages stabilize, and E_\infty is the one of [def-sp-convergence] appearing in clause (b) of [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields]).

source.place: Lemma-spectral-sequence-filtered-complex-functorial and the page-by-page comparison argument following Tag 0BDU

proof.text: For each total degree n, the convergence clause (b) of [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] identifies E_\infty^{p,n-p} with the graded piece of the finite induced filtration on H^n(C\otimes_A B) and on H^n(D), and H^n(u):H^n(C\otimes_A B)\to H^n(D) is a filtered map on these abutments inducing the E_\infty map. Step 2 gives an isomorphism on every graded piece. Apply [lem-sp-finite-filtration-induction] to this filtered map; its finite-filtration hypothesis holds by clause (b). Hence H^n(C\otimes_A B)\to H^n(D) is an isomorphism. Composing with the canonical isomorphism H^n(C)\otimes_A B\cong H^n(C\otimes_A B) of [lem-pc-flat-tensor-complex-cohom] (an elementary remark: $H^i$ of a complex depends only on its terms in degrees $i-1,i,i+1$, so one applies the cited lemma to the bounded stupid truncation $0\to K^{i-1}\to K^i\to K^{i+1}\to0$, which has the same $H^i$ and commutes with $-\otimes_A B$), H^n(u):H^n(C)\otimes_A B\to H^n(D) is an isomorphism for every n.
